Apple is about to launch its major new smart home offensive. A new report published today by Bloomberg reveals that Apple has three new smart home devices that are "nearly ready." The first two will be released in just a few months...

Apple's three new smart home products are about to debut

According to the report, Apple plans to release a new Apple TV set-top box and an updated version of the HomePod mini as early as this autumn. These products will look similar to the current versions, but will feature faster chips inside to support Siri AI.

For reference, the current Apple TV 4K uses the A15 Bionic chip. The existing HomePod mini is equipped with the S5 chip, the same processor used in the Apple Watch Series 5.

More interestingly, Apple's much-anticipated new smart home hub device is also "nearly ready." The report states that this product is tentatively scheduled to debut between "October and early next year."

Two versions of this product are currently in development. One features a screen mounted on a hemispherical base, while the other is designed to be mounted on a wall using a new magnetic attachment system.

Today's report also revisits the specifications and features of this device. It is said to feature a 7-inch square display, with Siri AI at its core. It runs a "new operating system" based on tvOS, and the interface is described as a "fusion" of tvOS and watchOS, featuring apps, icons, and widgets.

It will also support FaceTime, home security monitoring, HomeKit integration, and custom clock faces similar to those on Apple Watch.

However, the most eye-catching feature is expected to be facial recognition:

Finally, Bloomberg notes that Apple has two additional smart home products in development, slated for release at a later date. These include a "higher-end, mechanically structured version of the home hub" featuring a 9-inch display, as well as an "advanced indoor security camera."
